messages:
marta: Heads up — noticed a 3x jump in per-token cost for /chat-route between 02:00–02:15 UTC. Looks correlated with a single tenant doing large long-context batches. Dashboard cache hit rate dropped to ~5% in the same window. Anyone seen this? @devon @chris :eyes:

devon: Link to the cost panel? I want to see the breakdown by model and host pool.

marta: https://console.redwood/costs?range=02:00-02:30 — snapshot attached. Quick query I ran:
```
SELECT route, model, host_pool, count(*) as calls, sum(tokens) as tokens, avg(cache_hit) as cache_hit_rate
FROM telemetry.events
WHERE ts >= '2024-04-13T02:00:00Z' AND ts < '2024-04-13T02:30:00Z'
GROUP BY route, model, host_pool
```
Results show most tokens from model-rw-large on host_pool-b with cache_hit_rate ~0.05.

chris: This smells like a noisy-neighbor routing issue — those clients got routed to a host pool that doesn't share the KV cache. We had a policy that prefers cache-friendly pools for long sessions; did that change during the midnight rollout?

alex: We deployed sticky-routing toggle last night as part of rd/rollout-142 to reduce flapping. It was intended to be transparent, but IIRC we added a host affinity override for certain customer tags. @devon was that the canary?

devon: Yep, sticky-routing flag was enabled for canary group. We didn't include a route-map exception for "large-session" customers. That oversight could force long sessions onto non-shared pools. My bad. :facepalm:

marta: If we revert or add the exception, how soon will the cache hit recover? And billing — the per-tenant cache credits will be off for that window. We need to estimate impact before contacting billing ops.

chris: Cache hit should recover within a couple of minutes after traffic migrates back to cache-friendly pools. But attribution is tricky: our telemetry assigns cache credits primarily at host level and then maps to tenant by active session. When routing changed mid-window, some credits were attributed to host_pool instead of tenant-facing route. We'll need a backfill job to recompute tenant-level savings for 02:00–02:30. Also sampling for long-context traces is only 1% by default — we probably undercounted tokens.

devon: Patch plan: 1) add exception to route-map to force large-session tenants to cache-friendly pools (will open PR in 10m), 2) trigger migration script to shift active sessions safely, 3) kick off backfill to reassign cache credits for the affected interval, 4) temporarily bump sampling for >8k context traces to 25% for 6 hours so we have better telemetry while backfill runs.

marta: Good. For billing ops: preliminary impact estimate from quick sums = ~6M extra tokens billed as uncached, ~$1.2k gross delta. Could be off if sampling is wrong. @sre-bot can you create an incident and tag @billing?

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-187 - "Cost spike: routing -> cache miss for large sessions". Assigned to @devon, @chris. Backfill ETA: 4h, telemetry sampling bumped.

alex: UX follow-up: console cost dashboards should overlay recent route-map and rollout changes on the time axis (small vertical markers) so we can correlate spikes without opening infra logs. Filing RED-312 to track.

marta: Thanks — once the PR is up ping here and I'll confirm the backfill scope with Billing before we run it.

devon: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/842 — includes exception + migration. Pinging now.

marta: ACK, watching.
